svg.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Operation
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Operation; subtitle: Build a qualified pipeline without promising a treasury payout.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four weekly milestones establish operating readiness, not first-deal completion. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–12 months. Pilot counts are workload targets rather than predicted engagement or collection results.; caption: Finish the month with traceable records, reviewed agreements, secure evidence handling, and an owner-authorized claim queue.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one jurisdiction and document the operating rules; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Choose a treasury and two property categories. Capture finder requirements, statutory event dates, fee limits, claim evidence requirements, and direct-claim instructions. Budget fixed overhead and document the funding gap.; label: Days 8-14; value: Configure secure intake and review twenty-five records; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Create a SQLite case register with stable identifiers, source links, access owners, and next-action dates. Test restricted uploads and backups. Manually review 25 public records to calibrate duplicate and identity rules.; label: Days 15-21; value: Test transparent outreach against ten screened prospects; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Where permitted, contact ten evidence-supported prospects without implying government affiliation. Explain direct claiming, document responses, and execute only agreements whose timing, fees, and signer authority have been checked.; label: Days 22-30; value: Prepare eligible packets and inspect the evidence backlog; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Submit only complete, authorized claims; otherwise log the exact missing evidence and responsible person. Review case aging, estimated contribution, and cash runway. Schedule weekly treasury-status and receivable reviews.

text.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Operation
text.tspan: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Operation

rect.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one jurisdiction and document the operating rules; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Choose a treasury and two property categories. Capture finder requirements, statutory event dates, fee limits, claim evidence requirements, and direct-claim instructions. Budget fixed overhead and document the funding gap.

text.title: Select one jurisdiction and document the operating rules

rect.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Configure secure intake and review twenty-five records; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Create a SQLite case register with stable identifiers, source links, access owners, and next-action dates. Test restricted uploads and backups. Manually review 25 public records to calibrate duplicate and identity rules.

text.title: Configure secure intake and review twenty-five records

rect.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Test transparent outreach against ten screened prospects; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Where permitted, contact ten evidence-supported prospects without implying government affiliation. Explain direct claiming, document responses, and execute only agreements whose timing, fees, and signer authority have been checked.

text.title: Test transparent outreach against ten screened prospects

rect.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Prepare eligible packets and inspect the evidence backlog; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Submit only complete, authorized claims; otherwise log the exact missing evidence and responsible person. Review case aging, estimated contribution, and cash runway. Schedule weekly treasury-status and receivable reviews.

text.title: Prepare eligible packets and inspect the evidence backlog

Assumptions: Four weekly milestones establish operating readiness, not first-deal completion. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–12 months. Pilot counts are workload targets rather than predicted engagement or collection results.
